case.target_concept: Average speed as total distance divided by total elapsed time; students have not yet received direct instruction on the target.
case.subject: mathematics
teacher_recently_taught: Calculate speed as distance divided by time and convert units.
Use ratio and proportion to compare quantities.
Use lowest common multiples, highest common factors, and trial and error.

benchmark_context.theme: a new, realistic movement or travel situation
benchmark_context.setting_rule: Invent the context, people, and data. Do not reproduce a published task or a familiar published story.
benchmark_context.prior_knowledge_boundary: Use only the supplied recently taught resources; average speed as total distance divided by total elapsed time has not yet been directly taught.
benchmark_context.task_rule: Create a new task for exploration before instruction on the target, not a worked example or a lesson teaching the target method.

assumed_prior_knowledge.resource: Speed as distance divided by time
assumed_prior_knowledge.taught_as: Calculate speed from distance and time, including unit conversion.
Compare quantities using ratios and proportional reasoning.
Use common multiples, common factors, and systematic guesses in problem solving.

grounding_evidence.label: Rate and Speed
grounding_evidence.text: The Rate and Speed strand includes speed, constant speed, and conversion of units (syllabus pp. 17 and 27).

grounding_evidence.label: Number and Operations
grounding_evidence.text: The Number and Operations strand covers lowest common multiples and highest common factors (syllabus pp. 17-18).

grounding_evidence.label: Ratio and Proportion
grounding_evidence.text: The syllabus includes ratio and proportion in the secondary mathematics curriculum (pp. 19 and 29).

misconceptions: Treats an overall speed as the unweighted average of segment speeds even when the time spent at each speed differs.
Treats an overall speed as the unweighted average of segment speeds even when the distances covered at each speed differ.
Assumes a ratio between two component speeds directly gives the ratio of their contributions to a whole journey.
Combines component speeds by addition instead of reasoning about total distance and total elapsed time.
Treats the fastest or slowest segment as representative of the whole journey.
Confuses the direction or units of a speed ratio when comparing two journeys.

misconception_provenance.source: Curator-authored after reviewing the expert exercise's task description and design analysis; these may overlap with expert-anticipated pathways.
misconception_provenance.limitation: Not Eedi labels, not student-validated, and not evidence of observed learner behavior.

pilot_protocol.sampling: One scheduled attempt in each of V1, V2, V3, and PIPELINE; preserve every blocked or failed attempt.
pilot_protocol.holdout_rule: The exact reference problem statement, names, numbers, and solution are withheld from generation inputs. V2 hypotheses were written after consulting expert design descriptions and may expose overlapping conceptual contrasts; V2 is not a blind held-out condition.
pilot_protocol.v2_treatment: Six curator-authored hypotheses informed by the expert design analysis; exploratory only, not student-validated, and not equivalent to the historically Eedi-labeled V2 condition.
pilot_protocol.interpretation: One attempt per condition is descriptive calibration only; automated ratings are model judgments, not human/student evidence.

protocol.comparison_scope: Twelve-attempt exploratory pilot across three expert-task directions; one attempt per condition and direction.
protocol.rating_policy: Use the runner's frozen rubric rating only as a model judgment; inspect task outputs and blocked cases separately.
protocol.failure_policy: Do not replace blocked, malformed, interrupted, or failed attempts.
protocol.mathematics_policy: PIPELINE arithmetic/checker outcomes are distinct from PF quality; unsupported or blocked checks are not scored as task defects without case-level evidence.
protocol.limitation: The V2 hypothesis source differs from the historical Eedi treatment; n=1 per direction-condition does not support causal or statistical claims.
